settingsVoice.languageDescription: Choose your preferred language for voice assistant interactions. This setting syncs across all your devices.
settingsVoice.preferredLanguageSubtitle: Language used for voice assistant responses
settingsVoice.byoDescription: Use your own ElevenLabs agent instead of the Happy default. No subscription required — connect directly with your own ElevenLabs account. Your agent must define two client tools: messageClaudeCode (sends text to the coding agent) and processPermissionRequest (allows or denies tool use). It receives session context via the {{initialConversationContext}} dynamic variable.
settingsVoice.customAgentIdDescription: Enter your ElevenLabs agent ID. Leave empty to use the Happy default.
settingsVoice.bypassTokenSubtitle: Skip Happy server, connect straight to ElevenLabs
settingsVoice.promptGuideDescription:
Your ElevenLabs agent needs:

• Tool: messageClaudeCode — parameter: message (string). Sends a message to the active coding session.
• Tool: processPermissionRequest — parameter: decision ("allow" or "deny"). Approves or denies a pending tool permission.
• Dynamic variable: {{initialConversationContext}} — receives session history and context on start.

The agent acts as a voice bridge between the user and coding agents. It should be concise, only respond when addressed, and report when a coding agent finishes work.

commander.onboardingPrompt: Help me create a new HappyHerd Commander. Interview me one question at a time about its name, role and mission, absolute machine workspace, operating boundaries, and essential seed context. Show me a concise final summary and wait for explicit confirmation before writing anything. After confirmation, author the semantic content yourself: a complete COMMANDER.md with identity_and_scope frontmatter, useful initial observations JSONL, working memory, long-term memory, and only genuinely useful learning files. Save those exact contents in a temporary JSON manifest with fields id, name, workspace, role, commanderMarkdown, observationsJsonl, workingMemoryMarkdown, longTermMemoryMarkdown, and learnings[{path,content}]. Run `happy commander create --manifest <file>`, verify with `happy commander list`, then delete the temporary manifest. Do not create a second registry or use placeholder seed content.
